solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dark-skinned couple making a bow

blocks.note: a synonym for dark-skinned
to couple is to tie or join together

explanation.surface: A dark-skinned pair take a bow together at the end of a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' looks like a gesture of thanks, but it is the knotted neckwear; 'couple' is a verb, not a pair of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal evening dress code takes its name from the black bow worn at the collar, so the phrase can stand for that neckwear.

clue.text: Like a cat, boy with that many lives?

blocks.note: Leo is a boy's name
a cat is said to have nine lives

explanation.surface: A catlike boy who seems to have as many lives as a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the lion, the big cat: leonine means lion-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means resembling a lion, which is one of the big cats.

clue.text: Rejecting some cappuccino for tea

indicators.note: only some of the word is used, so the letters sit inside it
rejecting suggests throwing back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the run of letters after the opening C, before reading backwards

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a coffee and asks for tea instead.
explanation.walkthrough: A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: In everyday British speech a cuppa is a cup of tea, so tea defines it.

clue.text: Backed some debate that is key on computer

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
only some of the word is used, so the letters sit inside it

blocks.note: the middle letters of this word, before reading backwards

explanation.surface: Supporting part of a debate that is crucial to computing.
explanation.definitionFit: The tabulator key on a keyboard is labelled with this short name.

clue.text: Opening special broadcast is work of bishop

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order
the mixed word opens up to let another piece inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be mixed
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A bishop presides over the opening of a special broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like the first letter of a word, but it means the jumbled letters open up to take in the short word for a work.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopal is the adjective relating to bishops, from the Greek for overseer.

clue.text: Fixed time in animal lair

blocks.note: set means fixed, as in a set time
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An animal returns to its den at a regular hour.
explanation.walkthrough: A sett is the burrow system of a badger.
explanation.definitionFit: The underground home of a badger is called by this name, a specific kind of burrow.

clue.text: Commits to notices being displayed

blocks.note: signs are notices on display
a notice that is up is on display

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to having public notices put on show.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up for something is to enrol or commit oneself to it.

clue.text: Point of fork catching wife's thread

indicators.note: something catching another holds it inside, so one piece goes in the other

blocks.note: a tine is a prong of a fork
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A fork's prong snags the wife's thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Twine is strong string made of twisted strands, a kind of thread.

clue.text: First course perhaps is very revolting

blocks.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
people in revolt are up in arms, or have risen up

explanation.surface: A diner complains that the starter is disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' reads as disgusting, but here it means rising in revolt, which is being up.
explanation.definitionFit: Broth is a typical starter of a meal, and 'perhaps' flags that this is one example.

clue.text: Fetches book and phones home

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
to ring is to phone someone
at home means in

explanation.surface: Someone collects a book and calls home to say so.
explanation.definitionFit: To fetch something is to carry it inside or bring it over, the phrasal verb in the grid.

clue.text: Huge performance by worker in charge

blocks.note: a gig is a musical performance
the worker ant is the standard crossword worker
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A supervisor at work puts on an enormous show.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives meaning of enormous size; a plain synonym.

clue.text: One offering treatment, the first to include music

indicators.note: to include means to take inside, so the music goes in between the other pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
1st, with the digit read as the letter I
rap is a style of music

explanation.surface: A therapist who first brings music into the treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The joined 'the first' is opened up for the music to go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist treats patients, so describing them as offering treatment is a fair paraphrase.

clue.text: Police force is back for support

indicators.note: something that is back is turned around, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
is shortens to 's, as in it's

explanation.surface: The police have returned to provide backup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police force is' makes the Met's, which is then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The stalk of a plant holds up its leaves and flower, so it acts as a support.

clue.text: Work over travelling round EU

indicators.note: things that are travelling are on the move, so the letters move about
the jumbled word goes round the other letters, enclosing them

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
taken as written: the European Union

explanation.surface: A report about a trip around the European Union, finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's whole body of work is their oeuvre, a French loan word.

clue.text: Make oneself scarce, grabbing right topcoat

indicators.note: grabbing something means taking hold of it, so it ends up inside

blocks.note: to make yourself scarce is to disappear
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone disappears, snatching the right overcoat as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topcoat' looks like an overcoat to grab, but it is the final coat of finish on wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnish is applied as the final protective layer on woodwork, the last coat painted on.

clue.text: Father fast making highest church office

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
pacy means quick or fast

explanation.surface: A priest who fasts rises to the top job in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' and 'fast' suggest a priest observing a fast, but fast here means quick.
explanation.definitionFit: The office of Pope is the highest position in the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Punch comedian and gossip

blocks.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw
a wag is a joker

explanation.surface: Someone hits a comic and spreads rumours.
explanation.walkthrough: A chinwag is British slang for a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is an informal chat, close to a gossip, the noun sense.

clue.text: Old musical that needs regular cutting?

blocks.note: first meaning: the 1960s rock musical of that name
second meaning: what grows on your head and needs a barber's attention

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a long show that needs trimming; the musical's title is also the stuff a barber trims.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1967 tribal-love-rock musical bears this title, and the growth on the scalp needs periodic trimming.

clue.text: Wife finally opening a can, enjoyed home cooking?

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept
opening a container means getting inside it, so the letter goes within

blocks.note: taken as written
a tin is a can
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A wife at last opens a can of food rather than cooking for real.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony: opening a tin is hardly home cooking, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat in is to have a meal at home rather than at a restaurant.

clue.text: Sensitive girl, Clea, all of a muddle

indicators.note: being all of a muddle means being in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, to be mixed

explanation.surface: A sensitive girl named Clea is flustered and confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone allergic reacts badly to a substance, i.e. is sensitive to it.

clue.text: Didn't get on a horse evidently for cattle round-up?

blocks.note: to have got on a horse and gone is to have ridden
O is zero: riding nothing is the same as not riding

explanation.surface: A cowboy failed to mount his horse at the round-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as RODE O, rode nothing, which is what 'didn't get on a horse' means.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo was originally a round-up of cattle; the question mark flags the looser modern show sense.

clue.text: Alcohol I consumed at food counter in a frenzy

indicators.note: something consumed has been swallowed, so it ends up inside the drink

blocks.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop counter selling prepared foods
rum is an alcoholic spirit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone drank alcohol at the deli counter and went wild.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes inside the rum, and the deli comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirium is a state of wild excitement or disordered agitation, close to a frenzy.

clue.text: Frame of mind almost low

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the end is cut off

blocks.note: a mood is a frame of mind

explanation.surface: Someone's mood is close to depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' reads as down in spirits, but it is the noise a cow makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To low is to make the deep sound of cattle, the same sound as a moo.

clue.text: Married, rolling back years, appearing so fresh?

indicators.note: rolling back means turning the clock or a word backwards, so the letters run in the other direction

blocks.note: wed means married
Y is the abbreviation for years

explanation.surface: A married couple who look younger as if the years had rolled back.
explanation.definitionFit: A dewy complexion or look is moist and youthful, so the adjective suggests freshness.

clue.text: Island incorporated hotel

blocks.note: Inc. is the abbreviation for incorporated, used after US company names
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel on an island has been registered as a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island' looks like it should give I; it is the definition instead.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland an inch is a small island, as in Inchcolm in the Firth of Forth.

clue.text: Comprehensive, even if approximate

blocks.note: tho' is a short form of though, meaning even if
a rough estimate is an approximate one

explanation.surface: A survey claimed to be comprehensive though only approximate.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough piece of work leaves nothing out, so it is complete or all-embracing.
